title: The interwar years and World War II
note: Resentment of the 1919 peace and the Great Depression of 1929 helped dictators win power in Italy, Germany and Japan. Their aggression was met first with appeasement, then war in 1939. The Allies defeated the Axis by 1945, after the Holocaust and atomic bombs had shown the war's unprecedented destruction.

read.title: From depression to world war
text: The peace of 1919 left many nations bitter. Italians felt cheated of territory, and many Germans blamed the young Weimar Republic for a treaty they saw as humiliating. When the Great Depression struck in 1929, banks failed, trade collapsed and millions lost their jobs. Desperate voters turned to leaders who promised order and national glory. Mussolini already ruled Italy as a fascist dictator, and Hitler became chancellor of Germany in 1933. In the Soviet Union, Stalin forced peasants onto collective farms and drove rapid industrial growth at enormous human cost.

The dictators soon tested the world. Japan seized Manchuria in 1931, Italy invaded Ethiopia in 1935, and Germany rearmed, took Austria, and at Munich in 1938 won part of Czechoslovakia. Britain and France chose appeasement, hoping to avoid another war. After Germany invaded Poland on September 1, 1939, they declared war.

German armies overran much of Europe, then invaded the Soviet Union in 1941. Japan's attack on Pearl Harbor brought the United States into the war. The tide turned at Midway and Stalingrad in 1942 and 1943. Allied troops landed in Normandy in 1944, and Germany surrendered in May 1945. Behind its lines the Nazi regime murdered six million Jews and millions of others. Japan surrendered after atomic bombs destroyed Hiroshima and Nagasaki and the Soviet Union declared war on it.
